title: Arrival at Bradbury Landing
objective: Get your bearings at the landing site.

objectives.label: Look around from the landing panorama

discovery: Curiosity landed on the floor of Gale in August 2012, between the crater’s northern rim and the layered mound at its centre.

title: Yellowknife Bay: an ancient lake
objective: Reach the Sheepbed mudstone and inspect the Cumberland hole.
discovery: The mudstone at Yellowknife Bay was laid down in a shallow lake, and carries clay minerals and sulfate salts alongside detrital basaltic minerals.

title: The Kimberley: Windjana
objective: Inspect the Windjana drill site in the Kimberley sandstone.
discovery: Windjana sampled a sandstone outcrop on the crater floor, the third hole of the mission.

title: Pahrump Hills: entering Mount Sharp
objective: Reach the first Mount Sharp strata and record the view.

objectives.label: Look around from the Pahrump Hills panorama

discovery: Pahrump Hills is where Curiosity first reached the Murray formation at the base of the Mount Sharp group.

title: Buckskin: the silica stop
discovery: Buckskin was drilled on the lower slopes of the mountain at Marias Pass.

title: Vera Rubin Ridge
objective: Explore the ridge and record the view.

objectives.label: Look around from the Vera Rubin Ridge panorama

discovery: The ridge stands out from orbit for its hematite signature, which is why the team spent a long campaign on it.

title: Glen Torridon: the clay-bearing unit
objective: Explore Glen Torridon and inspect Aberlady.

objectives.label: Look around from the Glen Torridon panorama

discovery: Glen Torridon carried the strongest clay signature on the mountain from orbit, and the campaign found the highest clay abundances of the mission.

title: Mont Mercou: layers of Mars
objective: Profile the cliff and record the view from the top.

objectives.label: Look around from the Mont Mercou panorama

discovery: Mont Mercou is a six-metre cliff of bedded sedimentary rock that the rover circled, imaged from several angles, and then climbed.

title: Greenheugh Pediment
objective: Reach the pediment and inspect the capping rocks.

objectives.label: Look around from the Greenheugh Pediment panorama

discovery: The pediment is capped by a different formation from the sedimentary layers that built the mountain below it.

title: Point Lake and Paraitepuy Pass
objective: Look back at where the mission began, then thread the pass.

objectives.label: Look around from the Point Lake panorama
Look around from the Paraitepuy Pass panorama
Inspect the buttes beside the pass

discovery: Point Lake looks out over Yellowknife Bay in the mission’s first months; Paraitepuy Pass is nine years further up the mountain.
